rows.label: A1
rows.name: The Universe exists
rows.statement: \textbf{The Universe exists}: the sole indubitable given (``I think, therefore the Universe is''). Neither axiom nor assumption.

rows.label: A2
rows.name: Infinity is incoherent in both forms
rows.statement: Infinity is incoherent in both forms, as an ontological posit. The actual: no coherent model is exhibited --- the completed totality forbids its own totality as an object, its antinomies are fenced and never resolved, its consistency unprovable from within (G\"odel II): the reductio with the four-class catalogue (5-red, Prop.~9). The potential: the undeclared \emph{freshness} posit, never registered: the idleness theorem and the truthmaker audit (29-fin). The successor act wraps (A7); the schema over finite instances is retained. Not claimed: $0=1$ in ZFC. The incompleteness face: 25-göd.

rows.statement: \textbf{Physical constants are definite Carrier residues}, $\Om$-hard to every bounded observer: the register $\{\dS,\Om,c,\hbar,G,k_B\}$ is generator-free in $\dS$ alone --- $G=2\dS=-c^2$, $c^2=2^{-1}$, $\hbar^2=-1$, $k_B^2=-2$, $|k_B|=\hbar/c$; the defining congruences are the observer's complete certificates, $G$ exact, the rest up to sign (B10); $h\equiv-\hbar$ is the per-cycle rebooking (D7). rows.name: The two-level horizon law
rows.statement: \textbf{The two-level horizon law}: hardness is one mechanism at every scale --- $\Om$-hard when the role lives at the Carrier's scale, $\p $-hard when beyond the Subject's own horizon $\sqrt{\p }$ inside its own shell; hardness attaches to roles, never bare residues. Lab-verified ($\Om=2{,}408{,}561$).

rows.label: B10
rows.name: One gauge bit closes the sign sector
rows.statement: \textbf{One gauge bit closes the sign sector}: no C14-type marker exists --- $-1$ is a square on admissible $\Om$, so square class is pair-blind, and integer parity is chart data (A8). Registered faces are pair-invariant: $c^2$, the one-way member synchronisation gauge (C8); $|k_B|$ (C12); $\{\hbar,h\}$ the two named unit faces (B7). The Hawking scaling forces $k_Bc=h$, so $k_B=-\hbar/c$ (chart-labelled).

rows.label: C6
rows.name: One frame group, three sectors
rows.statement: \textbf{One frame group, three sectors}: gravity's $(3{+}1)$ tensor, the Riemann observer geometry, and the quantum spinor structure are three readings of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\Om)$ --- its three tori the scale-time, translation, and boost freedoms, its order $(\Om{-}1)\Om(\Om{+}1)$ the observer variety --- the norm-one quaternion sphere is $\mathrm{SL}_2$ itself, the spin cover of the rotation group $\mathrm{PGL}_2\cong\mathrm{SO}_3$ that carries the cone chart (C22); continuum shadow the de Sitter $S^3$, a declared chart (C23) --- its spinor double cover the Clifford layer (D4). rows.statement: \textbf{Every Carrier quarter is a Fourier flip}: multiplication by $\gen^{(\Om-1)/4}$, squaring to $-1$, rotates the coefficient plane one quarter, exchanging position and momentum; both roots $\pm\sqrt{-1}$ sit in crossing class 2, since $(\Om-1)/4=\dS\equiv2\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 4)$: the flip chirality is the C14 bit, undecided by the Carrier. rows.name: The spatial chart is the 3-sphere (declared)
rows.statement: \textbf{The spatial chart is the 3-sphere} (declared): the frame torsor $\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\Om)$ (C6) carries one form on every shell --- $\mathrm{SU}_2(\F_{\p^2}/\F_\p)=\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\p)$ for the Hermitian form $wJ$, $w^{\p}=-w$ --- with the three element types of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, of which $SU(2)$ has one, all of finite order, and the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2=1$ and $ad-bc=1$ one quadric of $\p^3-\p$ points through the quarter-turn: the compact real form is no datum of the finite structure and cycle closure selects nothing. $SU(2)=S^3$ is declared the continuum chart of the frame torsor [chart]; given it, the spinor sign gives $S^3$ rather than $SO(3)$ (C22), uniqueness is Poincar\'e--Perelman [import], and the global de Sitter slicing has $S^3$ sections [import], the chart fixing $\Om\sim10^{122}$.

rows.label: C24
rows.name: The third-order wall of π
rows.statement: \textbf{The third-order wall of $\pi$}: for every prime $\p\ge5$, $\sigma_\p=\sum_{k<(\p-1)/2}\binom{2k}{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})$ satisfies $\sigma_\p\equiv0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{2})$ (Sun, JNT \textbf{131} (2011), (1.4)) and $\sigma_\p/\p^{2}\equiv(-1)^{(\p+1)/2}B_{\p-3}/36\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p)$: Sun's Conjecture 5.1, $\sigma_\p\equiv(-1)^{(\p-1)/2}(H_{\p-1}/12+3\p^{4}B_{\p-5}/160)\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{5})$ for $\p>5$, proved by Hessami Pilehrood, Hessami Pilehrood and Tauraso (Int.\ J.\ Number Theory \textbf{8} (2012), Thm.\ 5 (44)), reduced mod $\p^{3}$ with Glaisher's $H_{\p-1}\equiv-\p^{2}B_{\p-3}/3\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{3})$; $\p=5$ direct. Re-verified for all primes below $10^{4}$.

rows.label: C25
rows.name: The horizon is the origin's antipode on the boost torus
rows.statement:
extbf{The horizon is the origin's antipode on the boost torus}: for $w^2=
u$ a nonsquare (the drive $\gen$ serves), the torsor identification $\mathbb{P}^1(\F_\p)\cong C_{\p +1}$ based at the origin --- $P\mapsto u_P/ ar u_P$, $u_P$ the unique boost carrying $0$ to $P$ --- is equivariant, sends the origin to $1$ and the horizon class $[1{:}0]$ to $-1=\zeta^{(\p +1)/2}$; $\{	ext{origin},	ext{horizon}\}$ is the sign pair $C_{\p -1}\cap C_{\p +1}$ (C20), exchanged by the torus's unique involution $q\mapsto

u$ and at every $\p =4\kap +1\le200$.

rows.label: C26
rows.name: The four chains of 13-epi are E- and G-partial sums
rows.statement: \textbf{The four chains of 13-epi are E- and G-partial sums} [import]: the derangement chain $D_n/n!=\sum_{k\le n}(-1)^{k}/k!$ is the partial-sum chain of the E-function $e^{-z}$ at $z=1$; the arcsin and Machin chains are partial-sum chains of the G-functions $\arcsin z$ at $1/2$ and $\arctan z$ at $1/5$, $1/239$; $e^{\pm1}\in\mathcal E$ and $\pi,1/\pi\in\mathcal G$, both rings (Fischler--Rivoal, Comment.\ Math.\ Helv.\ \textbf{89} (2014); J.\ \'Ec.\ polytech.\ Math.\ \textbf{3} (2016), Def.\ 2). The factorial rate $\Theta(k/\log k)$ against the geometric rate $\Theta(k)$ of 13-epi E5 is the rate of E- against G-partial sums; a factorial-rate chain by rounding, $\mathrm{round}(n!\,x)/n!$, exists for every real $x$ and distinguishes nothing. Whether $\pi$ is the value of an E-function with rational coefficients at a rational point is a question of the continuum, not of the frame: the conjecture $\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal E\cap\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal G=\overline{\Q}$ (ibid.\ p.\ 37) would answer it negatively; the split of 13-epi E5 is by kind of chain and needs no such answer.

rows.label: D1
rows.name: Time is scale-dilation
rows.statement: \textbf{Time is scale-dilation}: each Subject rides its own drive $x\mapsto gx$ and assigns its own tick; a composite is read through the reader's one drive, so the diagonal action and its conserved offset are observer-derived --- the Carrier contributes no clock, the offset group fixed by the arena's divisor structure. Falsifier: a registered duration that is not a drive count of the reader's own frame, or a frame-independent Carrier tick.

rows.statement: \textbf{Mass is winding rate} ($E=hf$ an identity); masslessness $\Leftrightarrow$ drive-invariance; a mass is the non-split (Frobenius, $\F_{\Om^2}/\F_\Om$) component the drive rotates, masslessness the split-torus eigen-alignment. Falsifier: a rest mass with no cycle winding, a massless drive-variant state, or a stationary state whose registered frequency is not its winding index ($E=hf$ failing).

rows.name: Distance is decoherence

Falsifier: a metric separation not monotone in the decoherence count of the relational channel.

rows.label: D7
rows.name: A unit of measure is a reciprocal cross-frame relation
rows.statement: \textbf{A unit of measure is a reciprocal cross-frame relation}: observer counts per substrate count. Its atomic form is the action quantum, the Carrier quarter-turn $\hbar^2=-1$; its domain the unit-free order-four flag --- unitful measures carry it, observables are flag-free, the absolute unit value $\Om$-hard; the fundamental units the four domain horizons (10-dim). Constants: B7; arity: C12; windows: C13; commutator: C9. Falsifier: an absolute unit value registered by an embedded observer, or a unitful measure carrying no cross-frame reciprocal.

rows.name: The observable is a small residue
rows.statement: \textbf{The observable is a small residue}: a bounded observer reads only small residues, so an observable stable object carries a small exact residue (particle $+$ binding wrap) --- the confined hadron, the light nucleus, the stable atom; decay is frame-normalisation toward it. Falsifier: a stable observable object carrying no small exact residue --- a stable coloured state, or strong/electromagnetic proton decay.

rows.name: The unified sampling clause

Falsifier: outcome tallies over a complete joint recurrence that are not exact ratios, or a fixed-setting protocol sampling more than one stratum.

rows.label: D11
rows.name: The shell theorem (the Riemann Hypothesis over the holographic substrate, with D12)
rows.statement: \textbf{The shell theorem} (20-rh Thm.~hp; 20:E12, E9, Rem.~parseval): on every shell $\F_\p\subset\F_{\p^2}$, with no hypothesis --- the prime vector's spectral content is the constant mode with the nonterminal quarter-turn modes, the finite zeta vanishing on each; every mode lies on the self-dual line $\Tr=1$; the modes are eigenvectors of the scale-shift with the $(\p-1)$-th roots of unity as eigenvalues; the comb's Jacobi matrix is real-symmetric with the secular roots as spectrum. No off-line mode; $\Om$-blind, for every vector on every shell. Witnessed on seventeen shells $13\le\p\le173$. Does not decide the classical hypothesis: D12.

rows.label: D12
rows.name: The classical hypothesis is a screen value
rows.statement: \textbf{The classical hypothesis is a screen value} (20-rh Thm.~turing, Cor.~conditional; 20:F1--F4): RH below height $T$ is the count identity $\mathcal N(T)=N_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)$, $C\le N_{\mathrm{crit}}\le\mathcal N$ [import: Turing 1953; 20:A4]. Decidable per height, verified to $3\times10^{12}$; the uniform form is Z4. Falsifier: a shell window on which $\mathcal N-N_{\mathrm{crit}}$ differs from Turing's count.

rows.name: Observation is the Hopf section
rows.statement: \textbf{Observation is the Hopf section}: the Subject registers its past cone, one chronon per decoherence step (D1, D3); the cone chart is the Borel section, fixing the horizon class and moving the origin (C19, C22); the boosts move the direction, freely and transitively (C22); the horizon is the origin's antipode (C25), charted $\infty$ [chart]. Falsifier: a registration on the direct branch whose value is not the Object's drive state at $\chron -k$ for its decoherence count $k$, lookback read modulo $\p -1$, or a registration off the past cone.

rows.name: Mass is dilation
rows.statement: \textbf{Mass is dilation} (the harness face of D2): the boost factor of a frame's per-chronon step (C19) is its mass phase, one $Q_4$ datum with the winding rate (C20): the quarter on the spinor cover $C_{2(\p +1)}$, the sign alone on the norm-one base $C_{\p +1}$; the lab's harness flow is its chart between the exact $C_4$ stations, the pair class $4\gcd(\dS,2\kap +1)$ host-decided; rest energy the norm reading, $\ker N=C_{\p +1}$, boost-invariant (D2); gravitational time dilation literal: the static clock ratio is the register character $\gen^{-\Delta n}$, the exponential with zero coefficient freedom, $\beta=\gamma=1$ (C21, E4, D1). Falsifier: a static clock ratio between two stations not fixed by their register offset $\Delta n$ (the PPN temporal form, defect $4ab$), or D2's. Residual: the P1 bank (21-grav); extension C21.

rows.label: D15
rows.name: Thermodynamic entropy is the channel count
rows.statement: \textbf{Thermodynamic entropy is the channel count}: the entropy of the first law (E7) is the record $\dS=(\p ^2-1)/4=\kap (\p +1)=|\F_\p ^\times|\,|C_{\p +1}|/4$, one $k_B$ per channel, $S_{\mathrm{th}}=k_B\dS$ [chart], $W:=e^{\dS}$ the chart's microstate number ($\ln W=\dS$ holds for no shell count; the $k_B$ at the site is the chart's unit, not the residue $-\hbar/c$, B7). Universal attraction is the drive's single time arrow; the radiative sector gives two helicity-$\pm2$ gravitons at $c$, collective synchronisation. $G=\hbar c/m_P^2$, the channel's unit capacity (B7).

rows.label: P1
rows.name: The running floor: the shape a₀(z) ∝ H(z)
rows.statement: \textbf{The running floor}: the acceleration floor tracks the drive rate, $a_0(z)\propto H(z)$ --- a relation, $\Om$-blind, consuming no numeral of the Carrier, derived from the synchronisation floor $a_0=cH/2\pi$ (L1) under the gravity realisation (D5). Staked as the lead falsifiable prediction of 14-entr, 21-grav and 32-dark: the knee shifts and the Tully--Fisher zero-point evolves as $E(z)^{1/4}$. Falsifier: a floor constant in redshift, or one that tracks anything other than $H(z)$. The absolute normalisation is Z7's value; this row carries the shape alone. Confrontation (43-muse, September 2026): MUSE-DARK III excludes a constant floor and fits $A\,E(z)$ at free amplitude to $z=1.3$; the RC100 decompositions imply a floor back at the local value by $z\simeq2$, pending the full-curve refit; the JADES pairs at $z\approx7$ are degenerate with their gas.

rows.statement: RH, Goldbach, and P-vs-NP are the spectral, additive, and computational faces of one horizon clause: each a uniform check over the totality whose per-instance statements are $\Om$-blind relations (RH: D11, D12) and whose uniform form is an $\Om$-hard value (Z3, Z4) --- in no embedded reader's window on the physical Carrier, host-decided on a hosted one. rows.label: Z9
rows.name: No compression
rows.statement: \textbf{No compression}: quotational self-reference is unwritable over the finite totality (mention cost; per-symbol at every scale, arbitrary codings beyond a structure constant) --- the classical diagonal consumes exponential quotation-compression, infinity acting as the no-wrap idealisation; at the physical scale the compression threshold $t(\M)\approx1.6\times10^{125}$ symbols lies above the totality's registrable-state count $\sim10^{122}$, so no embedded reader reaches either side of the sub-threshold window (25-göd Rem. window); correspondingly, bounded-fragment truth is definable at polynomial overhead (the Tarski reversal).

rows.label: B2
rows.statement: Symmetry completeness (Thm.~\ref{thm:symmetric-completeness}): the fourth roots of unity form the unique order-four subgroup $Q_4=\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$; under the Klein four-group $\langle x\mapsto-x,\,x\mapsto x^{-1}\rangle$, $Q_4$ is the union of the two size-two orbits $\{\pm1\}$, $\{\pm\im\}$, and $\Fpx\setminus Q_4$ splits into exactly $\kap-1$ orbits of size four. For $\p\equiv3\pmod4$ no $\im$ exists.

rows.label: D4
rows.statement: Scale-periodicity (Lemma~\ref{thm:scale-periodicity}, in the field): $S_n(x)=x\gen^{-n}$ satisfies $S_{n+(\p-1)}=S_n$; the grids $G_n$ are $(\p-1)$-periodic as ordered lists; the zoom $[x,n]\mapsto[x,n+1]$ has order $\p-1$. As lists of rationals $x/\gen^{n}$ ($\gen$ lifted to $\Z$) the grids are not periodic: the periodicity is a relation of the field.

rows.label: D6

rows.label: E1
rows.statement: The framed complex chart (Def.~\ref{def:complex}): the pair $(a,b)\in W_H^{2}$ read as $a+b\im\in\Fp$; the quarter-turn acts on the shell as the rotation $x\mapsto\im x$ of order four; the chart is the plane picture of $Q_4$ acting on the shell, not an extension of $\Fp$.

rows.label: E2
rows.statement: The extension by $X^{2}+1$ is trivial (Prop.~\ref{prop:Cp-field} reversed): on the shell $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)\cong\Fp\times\Fp$ has zero divisors, $(X+\im)(X-\im)=0$, so it is not a field; $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)$ is a field exactly when $\p\equiv3\pmod4$; the quadratic extension of the shell is $\Fp[\eta]$, $\eta^{2}=\nu$ a non-square (8-dirac B6).

rows.label: Y1
rows.statement: Solving in the substrate (first clause): $f\in\Fp[X]$ has a root in $\Fp$ iff $f$ and $X^{\p}-X=\prod_{a}(X-a)$ are not coprime; the gcd counts the distinct roots and Cantor--Zassenhaus splitting finds them, exactly. An equation without a root in $\Fp$ is recognised, not extended (E2).

rows.label: Y2
rows.statement: Limit-like approximation (second clause), across the tower: for every real $r$ and $\varepsilon>0$ some shell $\p=4\kap+1$ carries a framed rational $x/2^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, within $\varepsilon$ of $r$ (primes $\equiv1\pmod4$ beyond every bound). One shell resolves to D5's bound; the limit is the tower, not a completion.

rows.label: Y3
rows.statement: Continuous symmetry, the abelian case (third clause): $\Fpx\simeq C_{\p-1}\simeq SO(2,\Fp)$ (6:E2) is a $\pi/(\p-1)$-net of $U(1)$ under $k\mapsto e^{2\pi\im k/(\p-1)}$; the rounding $k(\theta)=\lfloor(\p-1)\theta/2\pi+\tfrac12\rfloor$ has angle and chord error $\le\pi/(\p-1)$ and group-law defect at most one step.

rows.label: Y4
rows.statement: Continuous symmetry, the non-abelian obstruction: no finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ is an $\varepsilon$-net for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0=\arccos\big((3\sqrt5-1)/8\big)\approx44.5^\circ$, the covering radius of the icosahedral group (A3); the tetrahedral, cyclic and dihedral groups have radius $\ge\pi/2$, the octahedral $\approx62.8^\circ$. Finite subgroups cannot approximate $SO(3)$; the window does (Y5).

rows.label: Y5
rows.statement: Continuous symmetry, the non-abelian case resolved by the window: the framed quaternions $W_H^{4}$, read in a shell $\p>8H^{2}$, compose exactly (products land in $W_{4H^{2}}$); normalised, they are an $\varepsilon$-net of $SO(3)$ with $\varepsilon\le2\arcsin(1/H)$ (round $Hs$ to the lattice). At $H=3$, $\p=73$: $38.9^\circ<\varepsilon_0$, finer than any finite subgroup; measured $30.0^\circ$.

rows.label: Y6
rows.statement: The conjecture of the conclusion, what remains after Y1--Y5: the Lie-algebra layer --- one-parameter subgroups and their generators inside the window, where iterating a window rotation $m$ times consumes range as $H^{2m}$; whether the Cayley step of 8-dirac (8:C4) supplies exact one-parameter subgroups of the window net on every shell is open.

rows.label: Z1
rows.statement: No element of additive order two (Thm.~\ref{thm:no-south-pole}): $2s=0$ forces $s=0$; the antipode of the origin on the additive cycle is not a residue; it sits between $2\kap=(\p-1)/2$ and $2\kap+1=(\p+1)/2=2^{-1}$ (20-rh B8).

rows.label: Z2
rows.statement: The antipode named $\infty$: the horizon of the observer at $0$ (00:C25, 00:D13), the compactification point of the framed line [chart]; its reading as classical infinity is the chart, not a residue.

rows.label: A1
rows.statement: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$; its generators are the $\gen^{u}$, $u\in\Zp^{\times}$; $\gen^{(\p-1)/2}=-1$; $-1$ is a square in $\Fp$ iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$; the fourth roots of unity form the unique subgroup of order four (1:A1, 1:B2).

rows.label: A2
rows.statement: The sign of the quarter-turn exponent: $\im=\gen^{-\kap}=-\gen^{\kap}$, the exponent negative by pullback covariance (00:C7); the positive-exponent reading is the conjugate chart. Declared here, derived in the corpus.

rows.label: A3
rows.statement: Topology: a closed connected surface with Euler characteristic $2$ is the two-sphere; the suspension of a circle is $S^{2}$ (Hatcher, Ex.~0.14); a quotient of a regular CW complex by a subcomplex is a CW complex.

rows.label: A4
rows.statement: The framed-rational charts of 1-algebra: on one shell the scale grids $x/\gen^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, trade range for resolution (1:D5); across shells the tower resolves every real (1:Y2).

rows.label: B1
rows.statement: The shell $(\kap,\Fp)$, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$ prime; the half-period $\pi:=2\kap$; the meridian steps $I_{\p}=\{0,\dots,\pi\}$; the phase cycle $\Phi_{\p}\cong C_{\p-1}$, $m\mapsto\gen^{m}$ (Defs.~\ref{def:prime-shell}, \ref{def:half-period}; 00:C1).

rows.label: B2
rows.statement: The frame $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$: origin, unit, and the Subject's drive generator $\gen$, a primitive generator of $\Fpx$; $\chron$ the chronon (00:C1, convention~3).

rows.label: B3
rows.statement: Primitive generators form one orbit: every generator is $\gen^{u}$ with $u\in\Zp^{\times}$, a torsor for $\operatorname{Aut}(C_{\p-1})$ (Props.~\ref{prop:primitive-orbit}, \ref{prop:no-canonical-e}).

rows.label: B4
rows.statement: Cellular automorphisms of the index grid: $m\mapsto\pm m+c$, the dihedral group of the phase cycle; on the completion also meridian reversal $a\mapsto\pi-a$, exchanging the poles. The reindexing $\rho_{u}\colon m\mapsto um$ preserves latitude adjacency only for $u\equiv\pm1\pmod{\p-1}$; $\sigma$ is not a map of $\Sp$ ($\north$ one vertex, $L_{\pi}$ has $\p-1$); decided on $\p\le29$.

rows.label: C1
rows.statement: The orbital shell $\Sp$: vertices $\north$ and $v_{a,m}$ ($1\le a\le\pi$, $m\in\Phi_{\p}$), meridian and latitude edges, north triangles, quadrilaterals (Def.~\ref{def:orbital-shell}). The action reading $v_{a,m}\equiv a\gen^{m}$ is $\pi$-to-one onto $\Fpx$: the surface is two-faced (00:B11, 1:C4).

rows.label: C2
rows.statement: Counts: $|V|=\pi(\p-1)+1$, $|E|=2\pi(\p-1)$, $|F|=\pi(\p-1)$, $\chi(\Sp)=1$; the completion has $(\pi-1)(\p-1)+2$ vertices, $(2\pi-1)(\p-1)$ edges, $\pi(\p-1)$ faces, $\chi=2$ (Rem.~\ref{rem:cell-counts}).

rows.label: C3
rows.statement: Canonical spherical completion: collapsing $L_{\pi}$ to $\south$ gives a closed orientable surface --- every edge in two faces, every vertex link a cycle --- with $\chi=2$, hence $S^{2}$ (A3), on every shell (Thm.~\ref{thm:combinatorial-sphere}; decided on $\p\in\{5,13,17,29\}$ by exhaustive incidence).

rows.label: C4
rows.statement: Frame covariance: $\Sp$ is one complex for every generator --- the index grid $I_{\p}\times\Phi_{\p}$ with its step relations; the frame $\gen'=\gen^{u}$ moves the field labels, $a\gen^{m}\mapsto a\gen^{um}$, by the automorphism $\rho_{u}$ of $\Phi_{\p}$, not the cells. The map $\varphi_{u}$ of Prop.~\ref{prop:shell-covariance} is cellular only for $u\equiv\pm1$.

rows.statement: The half-period: $\gen^{\pi}=-1$ for every primitive $\gen$, $\pi=2\kap$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:half-period}); $2\pi\equiv-1$ (00:C1).

rows.label: D4
rows.statement: The exponential unit $\eu:=\gen^{\im}$, $\im$ read as an exponent in $\Phi_{\p}$ through its residue representative; derived, generator-dependent (Rem.~\ref{rem:exponential-unit}; 00:C1, convention~3); on $\F_{13}$, $\eu=6=\pi$ [value].

rows.label: D5
rows.statement: Orientation classes: for $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $\im'=-\gen'^{\kap}$ equals $\im$ when $u\equiv1\pmod4$ and $-\im$ when $u\equiv3\pmod4$; the oriented quarter-turn is frame-covariant within one class of generators, not under every generator change.

rows.label: D6
rows.statement: The Euler identity on the shell: $\eu^{\im\pi}=\gen^{2\kap\im^{2}}=(-1)^{\im}$, equal to $-1$ exactly when the representative of $\im$ is odd (00:C14); the oriented frames of a shell are those with $-\gen^{\kap}$ odd --- on $\F_{13}$, $\gen=2$ ($\im=5$) is one, on $\F_{17}$, $\gen=3$ ($\im=4$) is not.

rows.label: D7
rows.statement: Negation $R(x)=-x$ and inversion $I(x)=x^{-1}$ are commuting involutions; off $\Qp$ the $\langle R,I\rangle$-orbit $\{x,-x,x^{-1},-x^{-1}\}$ has four elements, and $\Fpx\setminus\Qp$ splits into $\kap-1$ such orbits (Props.~\ref{prop:shell-negation}, \ref{prop:k4-shell}; 1:B2).

rows.label: D8
rows.statement: Euclidean conjugation $C_{\gen}\colon(a,b)\mapsto(a,-b)$ is an involution of the coordinate pairs $\Fp^{2}$; on the shell $a+b\im$ is a field element and the pair map $\Fp^{2}\to\Fp$ is $\p$-to-one (1:E2), so $C_{\gen}$ is a chart-level involution, not a field automorphism.

rows.label: E1
rows.statement: The comparison map $\Xi_{\p,\gen}$ [chart]: $\north\mapsto(0,0,1)$, $v_{a,m}\mapsto(\sin\theta_{a}\cos\phi_{m},\sin\theta_{a}\sin\phi_{m},\cos\theta_{a})$ with $\theta_{a}=\pi_{\R}a/(2\kap)$, $\phi_{m}=2\pi_{\R}m/(\p-1)$, $\pi_{\R}$ the chart constant (00:N2); $L_{\pi}\mapsto(0,0,-1)$ (Def.~\ref{def:realization-map}).

rows.label: E3
rows.statement: Fixed-shell refinement is bounded: with $m=\lfloor\log_{\gen}(2\kap+1)\rfloor$ no point $x/\gen^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, lies in $(\max(1-\gen^{-m},2\kap\gen^{-m-1}),1)$ at any depth, so the covering radius of the scale grid in $[0,1]$ is $\ge\tfrac12\min(\gen^{-m},1-2\kap\gen^{-m-1})$ for every $N$: $1/8$ at $(13,2)$, $5/22$ at $(13,11)$.

rows.label: F1
rows.statement: $\gen$ is a principal $n$-th root of unity, $n=\p-1$: $\gen^{n}=1$, $\sum_{j<n}\gen^{jk}=0$ for $0<k<n$, and $n^{-1}=-1$ in $\Fp$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:principal-root}; $2\pi\equiv-1$).

rows.label: F2
rows.statement: The ring Fourier transform on the phase cycle: $\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}=\sum_{j<n}v_{j}\gen^{jk}$ on $V_{\gen}=\Fp^{n}$; the matrix $(W_{\gen})_{kj}=\gen^{jk}$ (Def.~\ref{def:ring-dft}, Rem.~\ref{rem:dft-matrix}).

rows.label: F3
rows.statement: Inversion: $v_{j}=-\sum_{k<n}\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}\gen^{-jk}$, i.e.\ $W_{\gen}^{-1}=-(\gen^{-jk})_{jk}=-W_{\gen}J$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:ring-dft-inverse}; 6:B5), exact on every shell.

rows.label: F4
rows.statement: Polynomial reading: $\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}=P_{v}(\gen^{k})$ with $P_{v}=\sum_{j}v_{j}X^{j}$; the transform exchanges coefficients with values on the phase cycle (Prop.~\ref{prop:polynomial-form}).

rows.label: F5
rows.statement: Covariance under generator change: for $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $v^{(\gen')}_{j}=v^{(\gen)}_{uj}$ and $\mathcal F_{\gen'}(v^{(\gen')})=\mathcal F_{\gen}(v^{(\gen)})$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:ring-dft-covariance}).

rows.label: F6
rows.statement: Exact external transport [chart]: $\chi(\gen^{m})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}\im m/n}$ is an isomorphism of $\Fpx$ onto the complex $n$-th roots of unity with $\chi(\gen^{m+1})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}\im/n}\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\gen^{m+\pi})=-\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\im\gen^{m})=\im\,\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\gen^{jr})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}\im jr/n}$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:datum-role-transport}).

rows.label: F7
rows.statement: The large-$\p$ reading [chart]: the phase cycle read as the $n$-point grid $\phi_{m}=2\pi_{\R}m/n$ on $S^{1}$; the classical sampled DFT, exact recovery for $n>2N$, and trapezoidal convergence are the degenerate comparison case, imported (Rem.~\ref{rem:observer-fourier-contact}).

rows.label: A1
rows.statement:
Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$ with two square classes $S=(\Fpx)^{2}$ and $N=\Fpx\setminus S$ of $(\p-1)/2$ each; $-1\in S$ for $\p\equiv1\pmod4$; $X^{2}-
u$ is irreducible for $
u\in N$ and $\Fpq=\Fp(\sqrt
u)$; every element of $\Fp$ is a square in $\Fpq$.

rows.label: A2
rows.statement: Quadratic forms over finite fields of odd characteristic: nondegenerate forms are classified by dimension and discriminant, isotropic in dimension three and more; in dimension four the hyperbolic type (discriminant a square, Witt index two, $q^{3}+q^{2}-q$ zeros, $|O_{4}^{+}(q)|=2q^{2}(q^{2}-1)^{2}$) and the elliptic type (discriminant a nonsquare, Witt index one, $q^{3}-q^{2}+q$ zeros, $|O_{4}^{-}(q)|=2q^{2}(q^{4}-1)$); Witt's theorem.

rows.label: A3
rows.statement: The framed substrate: the shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with frame $(\chron;0,1,\g)$ and quarter-turn $\im=-\g^{\kap}$ (1:B2, B3); the square class as drive-step parity, the drive $\g$ a nonsquare on every shell, $\nu=\g$ canonical (8:B3, B5; 00:C8); the boost cycle as the non-split torus (8:D5; 22:A2).

rows.label: A4
rows.statement: The continuum comparison: Minkowski's form $-c^{2}t^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ of signature $(1,3)$ and Witt index one over $\R$, its Lorentz group $O(1,3)$; the ordering of $\R$ that finite fields lack.

rows.label: B2
rows.statement: Nonexistence of a causal square root: no $c\in\Fp$ has $c^{2}=\nu$ for $\nu\in N$; for $c\in\Fpx$ every coefficient of $-c^{2}t^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ is a square ($-1=\im^{2}$), the form Euclidean with $\p^{3}+\p^{2}-\p$ zeros; $c=0$ gives a degenerate form.

rows.label: B3
rows.statement: Square-class absorption: if $a_{i}/a_{0}\in S$ for all $\im$ then $Q\simeq a_{0}\sum Y_{i}^{2}$ by $Y_{i}=w_{i}X_{i}$, $w_{i}^{2}=a_{i}/a_{0}$; no root of $a_{0}$ is needed, and none exists for $a_{0}\in N$ ($-a_{0}$ is a nonsquare with it).

rows.label: E1

rows.label: A1
rows.statement: Finite sets and maps: a map between finite sets of equal cardinality is injective exactly when it is bijective; a set of cardinality at most $|U|$ injects into $U$; unique factorisation in $\Z$ (the Gödel code).

rows.text: The latent domain: a finite set $\mathcal Z\subset\mathcal U_t=\Fp$, the complete relational domain a model reconstructs from its data; the shell is the ambient set and a reading of it is a projection (00:A6). Def. def:latent; Section sec:framework

rows.label: B2
rows.statement: Observation maps: $g_m:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X_m$ deterministic, one per modality, carrying its resolution; no stochastic model and no conditional independence is assumed; every cross-modal relation factors through $\mathcal Z$.
rows.text: Observation maps: $g_m:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X_m$ deterministic, one per modality, carrying its resolution; no stochastic model and no conditional independence is assumed; every cross-modal relation factors through $\mathcal Z$. Eq. eq:obsmap; Eq. eq:obsmapBackground

rows.label: B3
rows.statement: Adequacy: $E_m:\mathcal X_m\to W_m$ is adequate when $E_m\circ g_m=\varphi_m$ is a bijection $\mathcal Z\to W_m$; minimality, $W_m=\varphi_m(\mathcal Z)$, is part of the bijection, so the minimal adequate representation of Section~\ref{sec:background} and Definition~\ref{def:adequate} are one notion.

Def. def:adequate

rows.label: B4
rows.statement: Adequacy makes the observation map injective on the latent domain: $g_m(z)=g_m(z')$ forces $z=z'$; $\mathcal Z$ is the domain modality $m$ resolves completely.
rows.text: Adequacy makes the observation map injective on the latent domain: $g_m(z)=g_m(z')$ forces $z=z'$; $\mathcal Z$ is the domain modality $m$ resolves completely. Section sec:framework p04008, FrcCore{B4}, FrcLedger{B4} Representation.adequate_inj, FRC.Representation.adequate_inj

rows.label: B5
rows.statement: Uniqueness up to bijection: for adequate $E_1$, $E_2$ of one $g$, $\psi=\varphi_2\circ\varphi_1^{-1}:W_1\to W_2$ is a bijection with $E_2\circ g=\psi\circ E_1\circ g$ --- $E_2=\psi\circ E_1$ on $g(\mathcal Z)$, on all of $\mathcal X$ when $\mathcal X=g(\mathcal Z)$; $\psi$ is the unique map with this property.

rows.label: B6
rows.statement: The embedding into the shell: $|W_m|=|\mathcal Z|\le\p$, so an injection $\iota_m:W_m\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ exists --- the one place finiteness enters; canonically $\iota_m=\varphi_m^{-1}$ followed by the inclusion; $\psi_m:=\iota_m\circ\varphi_m:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ is modality $m$'s chart of $\mathcal Z$.

rows.label: C1
rows.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:UST} (i), (ii): every chart $\psi_m$ is injective, and $\Psi_{m\to n}:=\psi_n\circ\psi_m^{-1}:\psi_m(\mathcal Z)\to\psi_n(\mathcal Z)$ is a well-defined bijection, with $\Psi_{n\to k}\circ\Psi_{m\to n}=\Psi_{m\to k}$ and $\Psi_{m\to m}$ the identity.

rows.label: C2
rows.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:UST} (iii): with $\iota_m=\varphi_m^{-1}$ every chart is the inclusion $\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ and $\psi(\mathcal Z)=\mathcal Z$; canonical structurally (unique once $\mathcal Z$ is fixed), not algorithmically; ``subspace'' means subset.

rows.label: C3
rows.statement: The canonical lift $L_m:=\varphi_m^{-1}\circ E_m:\mathcal X_m\to\mathcal Z$ satisfies $L_m\circ g_m=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Z}$, and $L_m(x)$ is the unique $z$ with $E_m(x)=\varphi_m(z)$.

rows.label: C4
rows.statement: Cross-modal consistency: $\psi\circ L_m\circ g_m=\psi\circ L_n\circ g_n=\psi$ --- observations of one latent state lift to one point --- and $\iota_m(W_m)=\iota_n(W_n)=\psi(\mathcal Z)=\mathcal Z$.

rows.label: C5
rows.statement: Charts of the shell itself: for $\mathcal Z=\Fp$ the charts respecting the arithmetic are the frames $x\mapsto a+bx$ (1:C2), $\p(\p-1)$ of them, and $\Psi_{m\to n}$ between two frames is the one affine map carrying the first to the second (simply transitive) --- the corpus's coordinate systems are the paper's charts.

rows.label: D1
rows.statement: Foundational embeddings are adequate representations of one finite latent domain: cross-modal alignment, transferability and semantic coherence are the bijections $\Psi_{m\to n}$ (C1), consequences of the shared domain, not of architecture; the empirical record (A4) is their registered consequence. Falsifier: two adequate embeddings of one domain with no bijective translation on the resolved states.

rows.label: D2
rows.statement: Scope and limits: the theorem uses the finiteness of $\mathcal Z$ alone, no algebraic or geometric property of $\mathcal U_t$; the shell as host is the ontology's claim (A3); optimisation decides when a representation is recovered, not which; non-stationary or weakly factorisable data may admit none; coordinate alignment may be intractable; nonlinearity as expansion and depth as shell complexity are analogies (Y1).

rows.label: E1
rows.statement: The hypersphere [chart]: a Euclidean chart $\mathrm{Emb}:\mathcal Z\to\R^{d}$ equivariant for a symmetry acting transitively on $\mathcal Z$ and orthogonally on $\R^{d}$ has constant norm --- $\mathrm{Emb}(\mathcal Z)\subset S^{d-1}$. The shell's character chart $z\mapsto(\cos2\pi kz/\p,\sin2\pi kz/\p)_{k}$ is such a chart under translation, $\|\mathrm{Emb}(z)\|^{2}=\p-1$; in the shell's arithmetic $\sum_{k}\g^{kz}\g^{k(n-z)}=n$ for every $z$.

rows.label: E2
rows.statement: Quantisation [chart]: a digital embedding has coordinates in a finite $\mathcal Q\subset\R$; at step $\Delta$ the distinguishable points on a sphere of radius $R$ number $N(R)\sim C_d(R/\Delta)^{d-1}$ (grid counts fit exponent $d-1$ at $d=2,3$); at fixed $d$, $\Delta$ the capacity grows with $R$.

rows.label: E3
rows.statement: Gödel collapse: for distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_d$ the code $G(x)=\prod p_i^{x_i}$ is injective on $\N^{d}$ (unique factorisation), and $G\bmod q$ stays injective on a finite set once $q$ exceeds its maximum; instance $d=3$, $x_i\le4$, primes $2,3,5$: $125$ codes, maximum $810\,000$, $q=810\,013$; signed coordinates are shifted first.

rows.label: E4
rows.statement: The reading of Section~\ref{sec:hypersphere}: the sphere is the continuous shadow of the shell --- uniform radius the absence of intrinsic attributes, direction the relational content; the coordinate count is a representational artefact, every quantised vector one element of one field (E3); the radius reads the resolved domain's size; Gödel codes establish representability only, not geometry or training.

No classical derivation is disputed.

rows.label: A2
rows.statement: Metamathematics: Robinson's $Q$, essentially undecidable, every model infinite; $\mathrm{Con}(Q)$ by cut elimination in $I\Delta_0+\mathrm{superexp}$, not in $I\Delta_0+\mathrm{exp}$; Tait's finitism; Dedekind's categoricity of the second-order naturals; true second-order arithmetic not arithmetical; Tarski's decidable real field; Solovay's model and Shelah's inaccessible.

rows.label: A3
rows.statement: Combinatorics and set theory: Fraenkel--Mostowski permutation models (symmetry as an obstruction to choice); de~Bruijn--Erd\H{o}s compactness of colouring; aperiodic tile sets and the undecidability of the domino problem (Berger, Robinson); Zermelo's choice.

rows.label: A4
rows.statement: The corpus: the totality finite and complete (00:A4), counting closes by return (00:A7), a bounded observer a proper part and every reading a projection (00:A5, A6), G\"odel vacuous over the finite $\Omega$ (00:Z1), the $\Omega$-hard demarcation (00:Z3); finite mathematics as ontologically primary (Lev, Zeilberger).

rows.label: B1
rows.statement: The standing hypotheses: (Eff) effective axiomatisation, (Arith) interpretability of $Q$, (Cns) consistency. Two doors for infinity: the meta-level syntax, potential and retained; and (IR), the object theory interprets $Q$ --- an injective non-cyclic successor with sequence coding, the completed registry inside the theory.

rows.label: B2
rows.statement: The bundle $\{$Eff, Cns, Cmp, IR$\}$ is inconsistent, with no soundness assumption: under Eff and IR the Rosser sentence is available, and Cmp decides it against plain consistency.

rows.label: B3
rows.statement:
Witnessed independence: every three-element subset is satisfiable --- $Q$ itself ($
eg$Cmp, consistent by finitary means, the superexponential cost exact); $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$ ($
eg$IR: consistent, complete, decidable, singly axiomatised, interpreting no $Q$ since every model of $Q$ is infinite); the inconsistent extension ($
eg$Cns); true arithmetic ($
eg$Eff). Four legs, all load-bearing.

rows.label: B4
rows.statement: The arithmetic frame $W_N$: domain $[0,N)$, constant $0$, order $<$, the graphs $S$, $A$, $M$ of successor, sum and product restricted to the domain (overflow fails the atom); frame truth is truth in $W_N$; a $\Delta_0$ sentence is transcribed through the graphs with guarded bounded quantifiers.

rows.label: B5
rows.statement: Per-frame completeness: $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$ is consistent, complete and decidable, axiomatised by the categorical sentence $\sigma_N$; truth in any finite structure is decided by evaluation, and the theory of any structure is complete.

rows.label: B6
rows.statement: Bounded stability, schema form: a $\Delta_0$ sentence $\varphi$ with bound $t(\varphi)$ has $W_N\models\varphi^{*}\iff\N\models\varphi$ for every $N>t(\varphi)$, each instance $\mathrm{St}(\varphi,M)$ a finite conjunction of finite checks; proved for an explicit $\Delta_0$ language with $t(\varphi)$ computed; Goldbach below $20$ has $t=400$ and value true (below $10$, $t=100$, decided by the kernel).

rows.label: B7
rows.statement: The unbounded quantifier is the internalised registry: a $\Pi^{0}_{1}$ sentence receives a verdict from each frame about its own domain and none about all frames at once; frame-relative completeness covers every executed verification (a bounded $\Delta_0$ trace) and no $\Pi^{0}_{1}$ closure.

rows.label: C1
rows.statement: The bounded agent of capacity $K$: records of at most $K$ symbols over $s\ge2$ letters, fewer than $s^{K+1}$ of them; certification is a retained record encoding a completed proof-check, one sentence per record, no schema compression.

rows.label: C2
rows.statement: No internal mirror: fewer than $s^{K+1}$ records exist, so an agent with $s^{K+1}<N$ holds no injective representation of the domain of $W_N$ --- a proper part cannot mirror the whole (pigeonhole).

rows.label: C3
rows.statement: Vanishing certified fraction: at least $c^{L}$ normal-form sentences of length $\le L$, half of each cohort frame truths by completeness, fewer than $s^{K+1}$ certified, so the certified fraction is at most $s^{K+1}/\lfloor c^{L}/2\rfloor\to0$.

rows.label: C4
rows.statement: The migration: without IR every sentence about the totality is decided and incompleteness reappears as a resource bound on agents --- the G\"odel sentence's role passes to truths whose shortest certificate exceeds the capacity; truth for $W_N$ is definable one level up (Tarski relativised to a resource hierarchy).

rows.label: C5
rows.statement: Horizon separation: halting for machines of bounded space $K$ is decided from above within $|Q|\,K\,s^{K}$ steps (a configuration repeats) and never from within (diagonalisation); Turing's theorem is an external non-existence theorem, classified with Cantor's, not an instance of the bundle.

rows.label: D1
rows.statement: The premises and baselines: AT (an absolute totality), IR (the internalised registry), AC$\infty$ (unrestricted choice over uncountable families); Cns, Cmp, Meas (the exact measure axioms of each geometry), and Det --- a totality decides every well-posed question about itself, elements, subsets and relations, with its full second-order theory effectively presented; declared as an axiom.

rows.label: D2
rows.statement: Antinomy normal form: Cns $+$ AT $+$ comprehension is inconsistent (Russell, Burali--Forti); the witness of Cns $+\neg$AT is bounded comprehension --- every set $u$ has a subset not among its members and no universal set exists, decided on $V_4$.

rows.label: D4
rows.statement: Choice normal forms: Vitali (countably additive translation-invariant measure on all subsets $+$ AC$\infty$ on $\R/\Q$, a countable amenable group) and Banach--Tarski (finitely additive isometry-invariant measure $+$ AC$\infty$ $+$ a free non-amenable rotation subgroup) are inconsistent bundles with distinct mechanisms; the finite witness is counting measure with definable choice.

rows.label: D5
rows.statement: The reductio principle: for each normal form a baseline $B$ and one infinitary premise $I$ with $B+I$ contradictory and $B+\neg I$ satisfiable by an explicit witness --- bounded ranks, $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$, counting measure (Solovay's model as classical corroboration); the rejection of $I$ is coherent and witnessed.

rows.label: D6
rows.statement: The selection thesis: every normal form conjoins completed infinity with a totalising operation (comprehension, completeness, total selection, a total measure); each is harmless alone, contradiction tracks the conjunction; classical mathematics rejected the totalising conjunct at each crisis, this paper the shared one, the selection settled by Det rather than convention.

rows.label: D7
rows.statement: Forced exit: Det supplies Eff and Cmp, so $\{$Cns, Det, IR$\}$ is inconsistent and, Cns and Det being constitutive, the reductio is forced against IR --- no determinate totality internalises an unbounded registry; the four-clause bundle condenses to this triad. Conditional on Det.

rows.label: D8
rows.statement: Finiteness of determinate totalities: in ZF with every infinite set Dedekind-infinite, a structure satisfies Det iff it is finite --- finite: the full higher-order theory decided by exhaustive evaluation; infinite: a copy of $\N$ inside gives an effective reduction of true second-order arithmetic, which is not arithmetical. The real field's first-order tameness is silence about its subsets.

rows.label: D9
rows.statement: Corollaries: no absolute totality is determinate (a universal set is infinite by the iterated singletons); Meas is decided content --- a Det totality decides every measure question, trivially on a finite one (counting measure). The totalising conjuncts of two normal forms follow from D8.

rows.label: D10
rows.statement: The three gates: syntactic infinity (meta-level, potential, retained), semantic infinity (a completed object of the theory, the target in all three forms), diagonalisation (a method, dangerous only downstream of the second gate); the paper argues with an unbounded supply of finite objects only.

rows.label: E1
rows.statement: Global choice on a finite universe: with a canonical order, $\operatorname{ch}(A)=\min A$ is a uniform pointwise choice rule; over a fixed finite base AC is a definable theorem; finite products are nonempty without it.

rows.label: E2
rows.statement: Periodic choice: an equality-periodic family $A_{i+N}=A_i$ has the choice $f(i)=\operatorname{ch}(A_i)$ of the same period; group-periodic families as equivariant surjections $\pi:A\to I$ with equivariant sections.

rows.label: E3
rows.statement: Equivariant periodic choice: a $G$-equivariant section exists iff each stabiliser action $G_i\curvearrowright A_i$ has a fixed point (one orbit at a time); the Fraenkel--Mostowski mechanism in positive form.

rows.label: E4
rows.statement: The definable basis: every subspace of a finite vector space has the greedy $\min$-basis, one definable function on all subspaces; the equivariant obstruction --- $\Z/2$ acting by $v\mapsto-v$ on the line over $\F_5$ fixes no basis ($-v\neq v$), over $\F_2$ it does: arithmetic, not formal.

rows.label: E5
rows.statement: Periodic K\H{o}nig: in a finite digraph with out-degree $\ge1$ the greedy walk repeats a vertex within $|D|+1$ steps and is eventually periodic with period $\le|D|$ --- the pigeonhole on an iteration over finitely many states.

rows.label: E6
rows.statement: Periodic de~Bruijn--Erd\H{o}s, dimension one: a $\sigma$-periodic graph of bounded range whose finite subgraphs are $c$-colourable admits a definable $\sigma^{m}$-periodic $c$-colouring (the transfer digraph $D_c$, its sub-digraph of vertices beginning walks of every length, E5).

rows.label: E7
rows.statement: The dimension boundary: in $\Z^{2}$ aperiodic tile sets exist --- every finite patch admissible, no periodic configuration --- and the domino problem is undecidable; the passage from finite admissibility to infinite realisability has no finite certificate, its demarcation none either. The finite reading asserts patch admissibility only.

rows.label: E8
rows.statement: The choice paradoxes vanish: on a finite set counting measure is complete and invariant, no decomposition doubles the set ($X\sqcup X$ does not inject into $X$), and every ultrafilter is principal; periodic variants inherit this on one period.

rows.label: F1
rows.statement: Ontology and conservativeness: actual infinity is an idealisation of the finite; the bounded fragment is kept exactly, the unbounded fragment in schema form; analysis as approximation over finite grids; choice in the small. Positioning: finitism, intuitionism, ultrafinitism, structuralism; the potential-infinity rule retained at the meta-level as a commitment, not a neutrality.

rows.label: F2

rows.label: F3

rows.label: B1

rows.label: B2
rows.statement: The class is the datum: $\Fpx/(\Fpx)^{2}$ has order two, any two nonsquares differ by a square factor, and the Lorentzian form depends on $\nu$ only through its class.

rows.label: B3
rows.statement: The drive is canonical: $g$ is a nonsquare on every shell and the only named residue whose class is nonsquare on every symmetry-complete shell; $\im$, $2$, $2^{-1}$, $-2$ are squares exactly when $\kap$ is even; $e=g^{\im}$ has no stable class; $[g^{-1}]=[g]$. Exhaustive on $\p<2000$.

rows.label: B4
rows.statement: The two speed-of-light seats: $\nu=g=c^{2}\cdot(2g)$ exactly on every shell; $[c^{2}]$ is even iff $\kap$ is even, $[2g]$ odd iff $\kap$ is even, the product odd always; the temporal coefficient is not $c^{2}$; anchors $\F_{13}$ ($2^{-1}=7$ nonsquare), $\F_{17}$ ($2,\im,e$ squares), and the laboratory Carrier ($c=171\,106$ base-rational, $1\,204\,281\cdot12=6=g$).

rows.label: B5
rows.statement: The square class is chronon parity: the squares are $\langle g^{2}\rangle$, a residue's class is the parity of its drive-step count; on $\kap$-even shells every element of $Q_4=\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$ is a square, so the order-four chart grading carries no signature. Exhaustive over every primitive root of $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$; Euler form on $\p<2000$.

rows.label: B6
rows.statement: Norm growth and parity: $N(gz)=g^{2}N(z)$ with $g^{2}$ a square, the single-chronon multiplier $g$ odd, $x^{2}=\nu$ unsolvable in $\Fp$; the flip $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ preserves the parity class.

rows.label: B7
rows.statement: Signature lives on $\Fp$: the Euclidean form has $\p^{3}+\p^{2}-\p$ zeros (hyperbolic, Witt index two), $Q_\nu$ has $\p^{3}-\p^{2}+\p$ (elliptic, Witt index one) on every symmetry-complete $\p<60$; $2353$ and $2041$ at $\p=13$; over $K$ every element of $\Fp$ is a square and the dichotomy collapses.

rows.label: B8
rows.statement: One-way and two-way transport: comparison (two-way) readings are even-parity, the one-way single-chronon multiplier odd, and the null-cone slope $\sqrt\nu=g^{1/2}$ is no base-field ratio --- light-like transport carries no registered velocity, only its square class. Falsifier: a registered one-way velocity, or a two-way constant that changes under the synchronisation gauge $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ (B6).

rows.label: C1

rows.statement: The Cayley step $U_{\alpha,H}=(I-\alpha H)^{-1}(I+\alpha H)$ for $\alpha\in K^{-}$ (the recursion $(I-\alpha H)\psi_{n+1}=(I+\alpha H)\psi_n$); the admissible set $\calA(H)=\{\alpha\in K^{-}:\det(I-\alpha H)\ne0\}$.

rows.label: C4
rows.statement: Exact Hermitian preservation: for self-adjoint $H$ and admissible $\alpha$ the Cayley step is unitary, and every orbit is periodic.

rows.label: C5
rows.statement: The finite Cayley transform: $\varphi(\lambda)=(1+\alpha\lambda)/(1-\alpha\lambda)$ is defined on all of $\Fp$, takes values in the norm-one torus $N^{1}$, and with $\varphi(\infty)=-1$ bijects $\mathbb P^{1}(\Fp)$ onto $N^{1}$, $|N^{1}|=\p+1$; the unitary group of one channel is $N^{1}$; the orientation gauge $\alpha\mapsto-\alpha$ inverts every $\varphi(\lambda)$ and imports the derived orientation of the shell.

rows.label: D9
rows.statement: The spinor form: under the plain conjugate transpose the gammas carry mixed signs ($\gamma^{2}$ the obstruction) and the $\gamma^{0}$-twist fails; $X=\gamma^{0}\gamma^{1}\gamma^{3}$ is Hermitian with $X^{2}=\nu$, commutes with $\gamma^{0},\gamma^{1},\gamma^{3}$, anticommutes with $\gamma^{2}$, and $X^{-1}(\gamma^{\mu})^{\dagger}X=-\gamma^{\mu}$ for all $\mu$; $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_X$ is nondegenerate Hermitian, $T-T^{-1}$ nilpotent and anti-self-adjoint, $\mathcal D^{s}$ $X$-self-adjoint and nilpotent ($\p=5,13,17$).

rows.label: D13
rows.statement: Mass is winding rate: the finite Dirac equation equates the meridional development rate of the spinor field to $m$ times the field, the finite seat of the energy--momentum--mass relation, $E=hf$ an identity. Falsifier: that of the corpus row it instantiates --- a rest mass with no cycle winding, or a stationary state whose registered frequency is not its winding index.

rows.label: F3

rows.label: F4
rows.statement: Two evolution sectors, one space: the split-phase sector of the drive and the norm-one sector of the Cayley propagators meet in $\{\pm1\}$ alone ($\operatorname{ord}(g^{-1})=\p-1$); the cycle Laplacian $\Delta_\Phi=D+D^{-1}-2I$ is self-adjoint, its Cayley steps commute with $D$ and the composite is unitary ($\p=13$); the dispersion relation $-\Delta_\Phi\chi_k=(2-g^{k}-g^{-k})\chi_k$; no meridional plane waves ($\gcd(\p,|K^{\times}|)=1$); $\mathcal D^{s}-m$ invertible for $m\ne0$, so mass is an evolution phase, not a kernel condition.

Falsifier: a registered dynamics of the shell requiring a phase outside the two tori, or a mass without winding (D13).

Prop. prop:h-domain, \Ssec:domains-flag

rows.label: D7
rows.statement: A unit of measure is a reciprocal relation between two count systems, counts of one frame per count of another; the unit flag is its domain form, the register crossing made algebraic; the Planck relation the unique interface introducing energy without a mass primitive. Falsifier: an absolute unit value registered by an embedded observer, or a unitful measure carrying no cross-frame reciprocal.

rows.label: E1
rows.statement: The quartet: the primitive triple $\{\lP,\tPl,\hbar\}$ --- the two anchored horizons, flag-free re-anchorings of the two primal charts, $[\lP]=\unitL$, $[\tPl]=\unitT$, and the crossing quantum --- with the dual horizons their crossed images, $\pP=\hbar/\lP$, $\EP=\hbar/\tPl$; the four horizons occupy the four domains, flag positions $(0,0,1,1)$; the pairing constants $c=\lP/\tPl=\EP/\pP$, $\hbar=\lP\pP=\tPl\EP$, $|k_B|=\pP\tPl$, and $G$ the one datum not internal to the square. The fundamental units are the Carrier's horizons. Falsifiers: a fifth algebraically independent relation within the quartet lattice; a measured variation of the dimensionless ratios of the constants.
rows.text: The quartet: the primitive triple $\{\lP,Pl,\hbar\}$ — the two anchored horizons, flag-free re-anchorings of the two primal charts, $[\lP]=\unitL$, $[Pl]=\unitT$, and the crossing quantum — with the dual horizons their crossed images, $\pP=\hbar/\lP$, $\EP=\hbar/Pl$; the four horizons occupy the four domains, flag positions $(0,0,1,1)$; the pairing constants $c=\lP/Pl=\EP/\pP$, $\hbar=\lP\pP=Pl\EP$, $|k_B|=\pPPl$, and $G$ the one datum not internal to the square. The fundamental units are the Carrier's horizons. Falsifiers: a fifth algebraically independent relation within the quartet lattice; a measured variation of the dimensionless ratios of the constants. Def. def:quartet, Rem. cor:domain-complete, Def. def:pairing, \Ssec:quartet

rows.label: E2

rows.label: E4
rows.statement: The defining congruences, pair form: on the Carrier chart $2G+1\equiv0$, $2c^{2}\equiv1$, $\hbar^{2}\equiv-1$, $k_B^{2}\equiv-2\pmod\Om$ determine the constants uniquely at pair level --- $G=2\dS$ exact, the quadratics each with exactly two roots $\{x,-x\}$ (admissibility guarantees the residues: $\Om\equiv1\bmod4$, $\dS$ even for $2$, hence $-2$) --- and the linkage $\{\pm k_B\}\{\pm c\}=\{\pm\hbar\}$ is derived at pair level; the root pair of $-1$ is $\{\hbar,h\}$ with $h=2\pi\hbar\equiv-\hbar$. Exhaustive on both Carriers.

rows.label: E7
rows.statement: The Carrier register is $\Om$-hard: no bounded observer resolves the constants' residues; the selection of a member in each pair $\{x,-x\}$ is a resolved fact of the instantiated totality, knowable to no sub-capacity frame (the window ladder, G2); the absolute unit values are read at the totality and their unit-face magnitudes are their only registrable manifestation.

rows.label: E8

rows.label: E9

rows.label: B2

rows.label: B3
rows.statement: The coincidence that forces the typing: at $\p=13$ the field element $6$ is at once $\eP$, $\piA$ and the reading of $-1/2$, while $\eR\ne\piR$; no map from a bare residue to a real number exists, and the external comparison takes the structural role as part of its input --- roles, not residues, carry external meaning. Witnessed by the two towers reading the same element $6$ as $\eP$ and as $\piA$.

rows.label: B4
rows.statement: Chains and their two lives: a chain is a sequence in $\fQ$ given by explicit integer formulas, with an external metric life read against $\R$ \chart{} and an internal residue life read through $\rep{\cdot}$; no third life --- the shell carries no completion of $\fQ$, and the continuum enters only as the chart. This is the statement of record superseding the framed-real construction of \cite{akhtman2025algebra}, \S4.4.

rows.statement: The registration quotient: at grade $n$ the observer forgets phase labels and cycle type, tallies all reversible relabellings of $n$ marks with unit weight, and retains only the coincidence predicate. The first of the paper's two \tD{} moves; not implied by cyclicity (the cyclic shifts alone give $n-1$ fixed-point-free relabellings).

rows.label: C2
rows.statement: The derangement selector: the registration statistics are generated by the rencontres polynomial $P_n(X)=n!\sum_{k\le n}(X-1)^{k}/k!$ (an exact double-counting identity), the normalised kernel $Z_n$ has $Z_n(1)=1$, $Z_n(0)=\dr{n}/n!$, and the unit registration ratio $R_n=n!/\dr{n}$ is forced; relative to the declared completion of $Z_n$ to $e^{X-1}$ the external value of the chain is uniquely $\eR$.

rows.label: F2
rows.statement: The wall identity and the terminal residue of $e$: $\dr{(\p-1)}\equiv\Ku{\p}\pmod\p$ (the odd-prime case of the Mijajlovi\'c--\v Sami congruence, A4), hence $\rep{\varepsilon_{\p-1}}=-(\Ku{\p})^{-1}$ whenever $\p\nmid\Ku{\p}$; existence of the terminal link on a shell is equivalent to $\p\nmid\Ku{\p}$, universal existence to Kurepa's hypothesis (Y1); re-verified in the derangement form for all $121{,}126$ odd primes $\p<1.6\times10^{6}$ with zero failures of either condition. Beyond the wall $n!\equiv0$: $n=\p-1$ is the factorial horizon.

rows.label: F3
rows.statement: Antiperiodicity: $\dr{(n+\p)}\equiv-\dr{n}\pmod\p$ for every odd prime and every $n\ge0$, so $\dr{n}\bmod\p$ depends on $n\bmod2\p$; the blind set $Z_0(\p)=\{n<\p:\dr{n}\equiv0\}$ always contains $1$, and Kurepa's hypothesis is $\p-1\notin Z_0(\p)$ for every $\p$.

rows.label: F4
rows.statement: Series duals at the wall: $\sum_{k<\p}(-1)^{k}/k!\equiv-\Ku{\p}$ and $\sum_{k<\p}1/k!\equiv-A(\p)$, $A(\p)$ the alternating factorial sum; the group law $\exp(1)\exp(-1)=1$ does not survive, $\Ku{\p}A(\p)\equiv3,0,21,28,132,258$ at $\p=7,13,29,101,257,1009$; on $\p=13$ the direct series residue vanishes ($A(13)\equiv0$) while the derangement side survives ($\Ku{13}\equiv10$) --- a second ground for the canonicity of D5.

rows.label: F5
rows.statement: Blind-scale statistics: over the $501$ primes in $(1000,5000)$ the sizes $|Z_0(\p)|$ distribute as $1^{(169)},2^{(209)},3^{(92)},4^{(22)},5^{(6)},6^{(2)},7^{(1)}$, mean $1.996$, the excess over the forced $n=1$ matching Poisson$(1)$ \apx{} (the model: $\dr{n}\bmod\p$ uniform for $2\le n\le\p-2$, the wall excluded; extended to the $1593$ primes in $(5000,20000)$: $1^{(597)},2^{(569)},3^{(299)},4^{(108)},5^{(17)},6^{(3)}$, mean $1.988$); blind scales never obstruct the plateau of D4 (advance at most $|Z_0(\p)|$ steps past $n_0$). The counts are exact; the Poisson reading is the model they match.

rows.label: F6
rows.statement: The $\p=13$ picture: the residue line $\rep{\varepsilon_n}$, $n=2,\dots,12$, is $2,3,7,11,1,6,\text{blind},2,8,10,9$ --- blind at $n=8$ ($\dr{8}=14833=13\cdot1141$) and terminating on $\rep{\varepsilon_{12}}=-(\Ku{13})^{-1}=9$, the common reading of $6/5$ and $11/7$ --- while the metric row freezes onto $2.71828\ldots$ by $n\approx9$: the thesis in miniature.

rows.label: F7
rows.statement: The fixed-shell tower of $e$: with $\delta_m=\ctr{(-1)^{m}\eP}$ and $q_m=((m\p)!+\delta_m)/\dr{(m\p)}$, $\rep{q_m}=\eP$ exactly at every grade (since $(m\p)!\equiv0$ and $\dr{(m\p)}\equiv(-1)^{m}$ by F3) while $q_m\to\eR$ with the certificate $|q_m-\eR|<(m\p)!/(\dr{(m\p)}\dr{(m\p+1)})+2\kap/\dr{(m\p)}$; on $\p=13$, $q_2$ differs from $\eR$ by $3.98\times10^{-26}$ and every member reads $6$. Compatibility, not selection.

rows.label: F8
rows.statement: The tail identity: $j!\,\dr{(\p-1-j)}\equiv(-1)^{j}\bigl(\Ku{\p}-\Ku{j}\bigr)\pmod\p$ for $0\le j\le\p-1$ ($j=0$ is F2); hence $n\in Z_0(\p)$ iff $\Ku{(\p-1-n)}\equiv\Ku{\p}$: the blind set counts the collisions of the partial sums of the left factorial with their total, $n=1$ is the forced collision $\Ku{(\p-2)}\equiv\Ku{\p}$, and Kurepa's hypothesis is the return-to-origin question of the walk with steps $j!$.

rows.label: G1
rows.statement: The legibility window: with $m=(\p-1)/2$, $\p\nmid\Cb{n}$ for $1\le n\le m$ and $\p\mid\Cb{n}$ for $m<n<\p$ (Kummer, A3): the residue line of the Wallis chain is defined on exactly $[1,m]$, blind-free below the wall and totally blind on $(m,\p)$; on a frame shell the last legible scale $n=2\kap$ is the angular address of $-1$.

rows.label: G2
rows.statement: The half-wall terminus, the calibration face: $\rep{w_m}=m^{-1}=\piA^{-1}=4\piA\equiv-2$ for every odd prime, the return statistics trivialising at the wall ($16^{m}\equiv1$, $\Cb{m}^{2}\equiv1$) and exposing the naked inverse scale; the identities are the calibration web of $2\piA\equiv-1$, and $\rep{w_{\piA}}\piA\equiv1\iff(4\kap)^{2}\equiv1$; the lower chain is blind at the wall and nowhere below.

rows.label: G3
rows.statement: The quarter-wall two-squares invariant: for $\p\equiv1\pmod4$, $\p=a^{2}+b^{2}$ with $a$ odd, $a\equiv1\pmod4$, at the quarter scale $n=\kap$ (the address of $\im$) $\rep{w_\kap}=\kap^{-1}(2a)^{-2}=-(a^{2})^{-1}=(b^{2})^{-1}$, by Gauss's congruence (A3) with $\kap\equiv-4^{-1}$; the invariant exists precisely under the frame condition; verified for all $211$ primes $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ below $3000$.

rows.label: G4
rows.statement: Second order at the half wall: $w_m\equiv-2+2\p(q_\p(4)-1)\pmod{\p^{2}}$ with $q_\p(4)\equiv2q_\p(2)$, exact to $\p^{3}$ through Morley (A3); the universal $-2$ persists to $\p^{2}$ exactly for the $\pi$-Wieferich primes $4^{\p-1}\equiv1+\p\pmod{\p^{2}}$ (OEIS A355959, G10), which are exactly $5$ and $45827$ below $1.08\times10^{11}$ \cite{oeisA355959}, re-verified here to $2^{35}$ (\src{pi\_wieferich128}; $45827\equiv3\pmod4$, so $\p=5$ is the only Subject shell among them; two below $10^{6}$ against the range frequency $\sum_{\p<10^{6}}1/\p\approx2.4$); the normalised quotients equidistribute empirically \apx.

rows.label: G5
rows.statement: Lucas revivals and self-similarity: beyond the wall $n\ge\p$ is legible for $w$ precisely when every base-$\p$ digit of $n$ is at most $m$ and $\p\nmid n$ (on $\p=13$ the two-digit revivals number $(2\kap)^{2}=36$); on revival scales $\Cb{n}$ factorises digitwise (Lucas, A3); at the first revival $\rep{v_\p}\equiv8$ universally and $v_\p\equiv8+16\p(2q_\p(2)-1)\pmod{\p^{2}}$ by Wolstenholme.

rows.label: G6
rows.statement: First-order wall vanishing of the arcsin chain: $\sigma_\p=\sum_{k<m}\Cb{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})\equiv0\pmod\p$ for every prime $\p\ge5$, $\sigma_3=1$ the sole exception; proved entirely in finite arithmetic through the key identity $A+B=2L$ (coefficient bookkeeping of the formal antiderivative of $(1-s^{2})^{m}$), Wilson reflection, Lerch's congruence and the binomial transfer $\Cb{k}\equiv(-4)^{k}\binom mk$. Verified for all $428$ odd primes $5\le\p<3000$; the ingredients for $m\le60$, $\p<500$.

rows.label: G7
rows.statement: Second and third order at the arcsin wall: $\sigma_\p\equiv0\pmod{\p^{2}}$ is Sun's theorem (A5), re-verified for $5\le\p<300$; the blind-range sum $\sum_{m<k<\p}\Cb{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})\equiv\p E_{\p-3}/3\pmod{\p^{2}}$ (A5), re-verified for $5\le\p<80$; at third order $\sigma_\p/\p^{2}\equiv(-1)^{(\p+1)/2}B_{\p-3}/36\pmod\p$ for all sixty primes $5\le\p<300$, the mod-$\p^{3}$ reading of Sun's Conjecture 5.1 with the Wolstenholme refinement, a theorem for every $\p\ge5$ (A8): Wolstenholme-trivial at orders $\p,\p^{2}$, Bernoulli at $\p^{3}$, the Euler content beyond the wall.

rows.label: G8
rows.statement: The $\p=13$ picture for $\pi$: $\kap=3$, wall at $n=6$; the residue line $\rep{w_n}$, $n=1,\dots,6$, is $4,5,10,9,6,11$ with $\rep{w_6}=11\equiv-2$ the calibration face and $\rep{w_3}=10\equiv-(3^{2})^{-1}$ encoding $13=3^{2}+2^{2}$; empty blind set below the wall, total blindness for $n=7,\dots,12$, first revival $\rep{v_{13}}=8$.

rows.label: G9
rows.statement: The fixed-shell tower of $\pi$: for $n=\p^{r}$, with $\delta_\p=\ctr{\piA B_n-A_n}=\ctr{-34}$, the member $\widehat\pi_{\p,r}=(2\cdot16^{\p^{r}}+\delta_\p)/((2\p^{r}+1)\Cb{\p^{r}}^{2})$ reads $\rep{\widehat\pi_{\p,r}}=\piA$ exactly for every $r$ (Lucas and Fermat give $\Cb{n}\equiv2$, $16^{n}\equiv16$, $B_n\equiv4$) while converging externally to $\piR$; on $\p=13$, $\delta_{13}=5$.

rows.label: G10
rows.statement: The $\pi$-Wieferich condition in three forms: $4^{\p-1}\equiv1+\p\pmod{\p^{2}}$ iff $q_\p(4)\equiv1$ iff $2q_\p(2)\equiv1\pmod\p$, with $q_\p(4)=2q_\p(2)+\p\,q_\p(2)^{2}$ exactly; Eisenstein's $2q_\p(2)\equiv-H_{(\p-1)/2}\pmod\p$ ($H_m=\sum_{j\le m}1/j$) makes it $H_{(\p-1)/2}\equiv-1$, and $(\p+2)^{\p-1}\equiv1\pmod{\p^{2}}$ identifies it with OEIS A355959 \cite{oeisA355959}.

rows.label: H1
rows.statement: The frame character $\chi(\gen^{n})=\exp(2\piR\imR\,n/(\p-1))$ \chart, the canonical external dictionary sending $\gen$ to $\zeta_{\p-1}$; the comparison map, never used to derive either constant.

rows.label: H2
rows.statement: The exact angular carrier of $\pi$: $\chi(-1)=e^{\imR\piR}$ exactly in every shell, for every generator and either chirality, since $-1=\gen^{(\p-1)/2}$ sits at arc fraction one half --- Euler's identity as the half-turn tautology $\gen^{2\kap}=-1$ under the dictionary, with no calibration and no error term.

rows.label: H3
rows.statement: Exact calibration of $e$ is impossible: with $\theta=2\piR\lambda(\im)/(\p-1)$ the frame angle of $\eP$, $\theta\ne1$ in every shell ($\theta=1$ would make $\piR$ rational, A2); $\chi(\eP)$ is a root of unity while $e^{\imR}$ is not, so the identification is intrinsically horizon-limited.

rows.label: H4
rows.statement: Calibrated shells at every precision: by A7, $\varepsilon$-calibrated shells ($|\theta-1|<\varepsilon$ for one chirality) exist for every $\varepsilon>0$ with relative density $2\varepsilon/\piR$, and $\chi(\eP)\to e^{\imR}$ along them; data for $\p<10^{6}$ ($39{,}175$ primes $\equiv1\bmod4$): $260$ shells within $0.01$ against $\approx249$ predicted, the best six led by $(\p,\lambda(\im))=(778933,123966)$ at $|\theta-1|=3.9\times10^{-5}$, consistent with the nearest-hit prediction $\piR/(2N)\approx4.0\times10^{-5}$ \apx{} (exact minima $3.93\times10^{-5}$ at $10^{6}$, $6.34\times10^{-6}$ at $2\times10^{6}$, $4.53\times10^{-6}$ at $4\times10^{6}$); the calibration inequalities decided as rational inequalities with $\piR$ bracketed by the Machin chain.

rows.label: H5
rows.statement: The null experiment: whether $\gen^{\lambda(\im)}\equiv-(\Ku{\p})^{-1}$ for some primitive root of either chirality is the index condition $\gcd(s,\p-1)=\gcd(\lambda(\pm\im),\p-1)$; over the $210$ primes $\p\equiv1\pmod4$, $5<\p<3000$, it is solvable for $94$ ($44.8\%$, against $96.0\pm6.6$ expected under independence), the correlation of the two angular addresses $-0.10$ at deviation $\approx0.07$ \apx: no invariant pointwise identification of the angular and radial carriers of $e$; the naive reading of $\eP$ as the number $2.71828\ldots$ is refuted.

rows.label: I5

rows.statement: The wrap-free window: an entity of the shell is $\p$-hard when it lies beyond the observer's horizon $\sqrt\p$; the accessible smalls are the natural counts below $\sqrt\p$, where sums and products of two accessible counts do not wrap, so primality, parity and order are wrap-invariant there and only there.

rows.label: J4
rows.statement: A framed transcendental is a $\p$-hard role with no bounded-height defining relation holding across shells; the chart shadow of a $\p$-hard role splits by its certificate --- a role pinned by a bounded-height relation has an exact algebraic shadow ($\im^{2}=-1$ giving $\imR$), while the half-arc and unit-registration roles, fixed by normalisations (C1, C4) with no such relation, have the transcendental shadows $\piR$, $\eR$. Neither external meaning, hardness nor accessibility rides on a residue symbol; roles carry all three.

rows.label: J5
rows.statement: Universality and the duality as corollary: $\p$-hardness is self-similar, every shell finding its own half-period and drive name beyond its own horizon, so the chart shadows agree across all observers; $\pi$'s seat is calibration-pinned with a height-two certificate and its arc role normalisation-fixed, $e$ has neither a pinned seat nor a cross-shell certificate and its role is generator-dependent --- structural against statistical is the certification split (I3). The sporadic small-height shells of J3 are the certificate-level face of I4.

rows.label: J6
rows.statement: Two constants, two walls: both attach their full-resolution shell content to sparse-prime problems (Kurepa non-vanishing for $e$, a prescribed Fermat quotient of Wieferich type for $\pi$); for each shell the bounded observer holds an exact finite certificate and holds no uniform certificate across all shells --- per-instance decidability without a uniform bound, the characteristic shape of statements at the arithmetic horizon; Kurepa's hypothesis is not thereby decided; the frequency of the persistence shells is a range reading (G4), their totality not a predicate of the paper.

rows.label: Y1
rows.statement:
Kurepa's hypothesis, $\p
mid\Ku{\p}$ for every odd prime, equivalently $\p
mid\dr{(\p-1)}$ (F2) and $B_{\p-1}
ot\equiv1\pmod\p$: universal existence of the terminal residue $-(\Ku{\p})^{-1}$ of $e$; equivalently, the walk $\Ku{0},\Ku{1},\dots,\Ku{\p}$ of the left factorial's partial sums does not return to its origin modulo $\p$ (F8). Open since 1971; the one claimed proof (Barsky--Benzaghou 2004, Thm.~3) withdrawn by its authors (2011); no counterexample for $\p<2^{40}$; re-verified here with the wall identity for all $121{,}126$ odd primes $\p<1.6	imes10^{6}$. Decided by no shell (each decides its own value: $\Ku{13}\equiv10$, $\Ku{233}\equiv69$, $\Ku{30089}\equiv5260$), by no finite search (F5's uniform model at the wall expects $\sum_{\p\le X}1/\p\approx\ln\ln X-0.24$ counterexamples \apx, so the model is scoped to $n\le\p-2$) and by no relation of this paper. Beside it, two large-$\p$ laws read on ranges: $|Z_0(\p)|-1	o\mathrm{Poisson}(1)$ (F5) and the independence of the quarter-turn index and the gcd class of the wall-residue index (H5; $94$ of $210$ against $96.0\pm6.6$ \apx).

rows.label: Y3
rows.statement: The large-$\p$ laws of the two walls, read on ranges and open as laws. (a) The calibration rate $\delta(X)=\min_{\p\le X}|\theta-1|$: exact to $X=4\times10^{6}$ (H4), $\delta\to0$ by A7; whether its order is the uniform model's $\piR/(2N(X))$ for every large finite $X$, the continuum bound being the irrationality measure of $\piR$ ($\mu\le7.1033$, Zeilberger--Zudilin 2020) \import. (b) The joint law of $(\Ku{\p}/\p,\ q_\p(4)/\p,\ \varphi/\piR)$ for large $\p$ (I5 on $\p<10^{5}$): $\varphi/\piR$ equidistributes (Hecke) \import, $q_\p(4)/\p$ equidistributes in the base at fixed $\p$ (Heath-Brown) and nothing is proved in $\p$, $\Ku{\p}/\p$ is Y1's; whether the three are independent in the large-$\p$ law. Each clause is a statement about every large finite $\p$ with the continuum as its chart, decided by no shell alone and by no relation of this paper.

rows.label: P1
rows.statement: \textbf{(Lead.)} The floor runs with the registered rate, $a_0(z)\propto H(z)$, the role statement of the floor closure, against both a constant fundamental $a_0$ and feedback-emergent scaling. Status: the constant-floor branch is excluded --- four redshift bins rising from $1.99$ to $2.71\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ over $z=0.50$--$1.28$ \citep{ciocan2026}, $\Delta\chi^2=23$ against $A\,H(z)/H_0$ \lcdm{} --- and the running form fits the bins at free amplitude ($A=1.39\pm0.03$, $\chi^2=5.4/3$); the binned rate sits on the $\propto H(z)$ chord while the authors' global linear fit runs above it, so the shape waits on the likelihood refit of the resolved tracks, and the amplitude's $0.12$\,dex excess over $cH_0/2\pi$ lies inside the $0.2$\,dex gas systematic. Falsifier: a likelihood refit or a wider-redshift sample excluding the $\propto H(z)$ form after the baryonic-mass and pressure-support systematics close.

rows.label: P3
rows.statement: The age--rate locus $t_{\mathrm{age}}H_0=(\pi/4)/\tanh(3\pi/8)=0.950$, exact for the realisation set. Read on the fit-independent stellar age ($13.61\pm0.34$ Gyr): $H_0=68.2\pm1.7$ km/s/Mpc \apx, $0.5\sigma$ from Planck, $0.65\sigma$ from TRGB, $2.4\sigma$ from the Cepheid ladder --- the framework favours the CMB/TRGB value at that significance, and forbids the $\Omega_\Lambda\approx0.76$ by which the rival chart would accommodate the ladder value at the same age. Falsifier: a confirmed ladder $H_0$ with the stellar age standing ($t_\star H_0\ge1.0$ against $0.950$).

rows.label: A10
rows.statement: The aliasing premise: the identification of the height coordinate with the meridian cycle (A1) carries the zero predicate, an off-line zero of multiplicity $m$ at a height symbol $H>2\pi\Omega$ is an off-line residue of multiplicity $m$ at the aliased height. The kernels $n^{-iT}$ share no period ($\log2/\log3$ irrational), so the chart carries no aliasing; declared, not derived.

rows.label: B1

rows.label: B11
rows.statement: Antipode dominance: in the units-chart basis the per-mode energy is $\mu^{2}(q)/\varphi(q)=1/\varphi(q)$ on squarefree $q$ ($1,\half,\tfrac14,\tfrac16$ at $q=2,3,5,7$), its unique maximum among the nonconstant modes at the antipode $q=2$, decreasing along the primes, not the modulus; in the additive transform the band nearest the half-turn, $k=(\p\pm1)/2$, is the strongest off the spectral origin and follows the same law [approx].

rows.statement: The staircase from the modes: $\Psi_L(N)=\sum_{n\le N}\frac{n}{\varphi(n)}R_L(n)\to\psi(N)$ as the bandwidth grows, the modes in modulus order, the antipode the first nonconstant one; the finite-bandwidth wiggle tightens monotonically [approx].

The bound uniform over every shell is Z5.

rows.label: D1
rows.statement: The dictionary [chart]: horizon $\sqrt \p\leftrightarrow$ Riemann--Siegel length $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$, half-turn $\leftrightarrow n^{-1/2}$, scale $\leftrightarrow\log n$; a shell of cardinality $\p$ reads $\zeta$ on the line to $T=2\pi \p$, one cycle of the shell, and a height is the scale coordinate of the shell that reads it, its count using residues below $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$ only.

rows.label: D5
rows.statement: Completeness criterion: faithfulness of the de-framing ($N_{\mathrm{crit}}=\mathcal N$ at every height), zero-mode completeness of the on-line spectrum for $v$ over the Weil class (A3), the absence of off-line zeros, and the Riemann Hypothesis are equivalent; an off-line zero $\beta+i\gamma_0$ leaves a residual growing as $x^{\beta-1/2}$ at its height.

rows.label: D6
rows.statement: The finite readings are approximations: at any depth neither reading produces an exact zero, neither uses nor supplies the hypothesis; completeness is stated in the zero-mode basis, and no transfer from the units-chart order of C3 is asserted or used.

rows.label: D7
rows.statement: The reconstruction is on-line: $Z(T)$ is real on the line, so every point it produces has $\Real=\half$, a property of the reading; the hypothesis is then the completeness clause of D5, the faithfulness of the de-framing, and likewise for each $\chi$-twist (E14).

rows.label: E1
rows.statement: The scale-evolution generator: on the shell the scale-shift $x\mapsto\gen^{\,r}x$ is a unitary permutation of $\Fx{\p}$ with the complex characters as eigenvectors; in the analytic chart [chart] the dilation group $U_r=e^{ir\Hh}$ has the self-adjoint generator $\Hh=-i(x\partial_x+\half)$ with generalised eigenfunctions $x^{-\bar\rho}$, $\rho=\half+i\gamma$, the symmetrizing $\half$ the half-turn of B8; the chart assignment is used nowhere as a shell identity.

rows.statement: Prime--zero duality on the scale axis: $\sum\Lambda(n)n^{-s}=-\zeta'/\zeta$, poles at $s=1$, the nontrivial zeros and the trivial zeros; the poles on the self-dual axis are exactly the on-line zeros, an off-line zero a pole at its own location off the axis.

rows.label: E6
rows.statement: The discrete eigenvalues from the comb: the raw count $\widetilde{\mathcal N}_N(T)=\theta(T)/\pi+1+S_{\mathrm{comb}}(T)$ carries the pole term (F8) and has no limit in $N$; the pole-corrected count $\widehat{\mathcal N}_N=\widetilde{\mathcal N}_N-\tfrac1\pi\Im[\Pi_N+\log\tfrac{s-1}{s}]$ crosses $n-\half$ near the zeros, its secular condition recovering the first ten heights to mean error $3.4\times10^{-5}$ at $N=10^{6}$ and $1.3\times10^{-5}$ at $10^{8}$; the raw condition stalls past $10^{7}$ [approx].

This is the sharpest divergence from supersymmetry, extra dimensions, and composite-Higgs scenarios.

The programme predicts these searches find nothing.
